Theme

Household, washing & chores · Nature & food

propagate verb

raise new plants from a parent

also layer (a plant), take cuttings, a layer, a cutting

classical

Cato Agr. 52.1 (Lewis & Short)
Col. 4.33.3: castanea melius ex vīcīnō perticā dēclīnātā propāgātur (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 17.96 (Lewis & Short)

propāgō, propāgāre, propāgāvī, propāgātum

verb, first conjugation

propagate by layers or slips

To peg a shoot down so that it roots; hence, to extend, to prolong.

Other words

  • propāgō, propāginis f. — a layer, a shoot pegged down to root

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 52 (Lewis & Short); Col. Arb. 7.2 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • sed truncīs oleae melius, propāgine vītēs respondent

    olives do better from stocks, vines from layersVerg. G. 2.63–64

See also graft, transplant, nursery, vine, sprout.

SourcesLewis & Short: propago

Vergil, Georgica 2.63–64.
